text: In JavaScript, accessor methods do not modify the array and return some representation of the array. The concat method joins two or more arrays, returning a new array. The filter method creates an array filled with all array elements of another array that pass a test, provided as a function. Filter does not execute the function for array elements without values. The includes method looks for a value in the array, then returns true or false. It accepts an optional start index, and the search value is case sensitive. The indexOf method returns the first found occurrence of the element being searched for, and if it is not found, it returns negative one. The lastIndexOf method returns the last found occurrence of the element being searched for, and if it is not found, it returns negative one. The slice method extracts a section of the array and returns a new array. It accepts two optional arguments. The first is the start index, and the second is the end index. If the start index is not provided, it will start at zero, and if the end index is not provided, it will use the array length. The end index is non-inclusive, which means that the selection will stop one index before the provided end index. The toString method returns a string representing the specified array and its elements. The elements will be separated by commas. The join method is similar to the toString method and joins all elements of an array into a string. By default, the separator will also be a comma, but here a custom separator can be supplied. This has been a 90-second JavaScript January.
